notes.title: We Need Your Help!
notes.content:
Good morning everyone!

We woke up this morning to find out that Steam has a new system for reviews. In an effort to curb illegitimate reviews and grey market key resellers, Steam no longer shows reviews of games that were done by an account that redeemed a key for the game in question.

In short, it limits reviews to only those people who bought the game through Steam -- no longer counting or allowing reviews of people who redeemed a key.

This has drastically altered the amount of reviews on Close Order, as many of our players who left reviews - both positive and negative - had been a part of our community from the very beginning (keys given at local events, some of our first people in Early Access), and/or were players who got it through bundles.

Today, we come to you all with a humble request: If you bought Close Order, please review the game for us! If you haven't played in a long while (i.e. before March-ish), we recommend playing again too. Whether you loved it or hated it, every piece of feedback helps us grow as developers in addition to getting our store page back to normal.

Thank you all again for everyone that's been with us on this journey! We're knee-deep in our next game Traiteur (which you should totally wishlist [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/470170/]right now![/url]) but Close Order lives on in our hearts and through our fans.

You're all awesome. Thank you so much. <3

- Your Friends at Raconteur

notes.title: Welcome to New Players! Tips from the Devs
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

The summer sale is upon us, and we wanted to give a warm welcome to the players who are just now joining us for the first time. :)

Close Order is a game that we poured our hearts, minds, and souls into -- and it was made better by your fellow players. 

Here are a few quick tips from the dev team before you jump in!

[list]
    [*]Always have minions -- you can't go it alone!
    [*]As you defeat more enemies, you'll rack up kills -- these kills eventually unlock additional slots within your armada. Start with 12, end up with 40! If a story mission is too tough, try playing a few rounds of our Survival mode to unlock more slots.
    [*]Every minion behaves differently, and different minions fit different circumstances. Be sure to read the advanced controls in the FAQ in-game for more! 
    [*]Don't forget that you unlock more minions by progressing through the game. Some players really like the Story missions, while some prefer to play endlessly in Survival. Each mode will give you more minions to unlock and diversify your armada, so try as much as you can!
    [*]Finally, share your screenshots of your badass armadas in the community hub. We'll post them on [url=facebook.com/raconteurgames]Facebook[/url], [url=twitter.com/raconteurdev]Twitter[/url], and [url=instagram.com/raconteurgames]Instagram![/url]
[/list] 

A few last tips: sell minions you don't like, try lots of different armada combinations, and most importantly... have fun! We loved creating this little world, and we hope you enjoy your stay.

Thanks everyone - let us know what you think of the game! :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Update 1.1 is LIVE! Play the Best Version of Close Order!
notes.content:
Hello folks!

We're excited to announce that the 1.1 update for Close Order has just gone live! See below for a complete list of fixes and changes.

Thanks to everyone who's given us feedback and helped us improve the game, especially those who stuck with us through Early Access. :)

Changelog below:
[list]
    [*]Drastically altered difficulty of first mission, should now be much more fair
    [*]Increased starting amount of formation slots
    [*]Added controller support! See FAQ in-game for controls
    [*]Fixed issue with audio options not always saving
    [*]Added options to adjust music and sound FX in addition to master volume
    [*]Added Quick Repair hotkey (R)
    [*]Added ability to switch between Custom Formation Editor and Shop Window without having to return to gameplay in-between, see FAQ for controls
    [*]Fixed issue in third mission with enemies sometimes flying through level barriers
    [*]Fixed typo in fourth mission briefing
    [*]Increased pickup radius for Prognosticator at end of first mission in hub 2
    [*]Greatly decreased volume of mortar sounds from standard mortar enemies and mortar bosses
    [*]Fixed Krewe minion render not properly displaying
    [*]Adjusted final mission to have a threshold of enemies remaining to allow for progress, such that players do not have to hunt down a single enemy that flew away in order to progress through the level
    [*]Fixed all minions being classified as "Offensive" in Formation Editor
    [*]Other minor bug fixes
[/list] 

This update makes Close Order the best it's ever been, and we can't wait to see what you think.

We're starting to turn our focus towards what's next, so stay tuned!

At Raconteur, we tell stories -- and your story is pivotal. We wouldn't be here without our players. Thanks to each and every one of you for your support of our weird, ambitious little game. It's been a long journey since August, and we couldn't have done it without your criticism, honesty, and support.

Check out [url=raconteurgames.com/stories] our website[/url] and sign up for our email list to stay in touch. :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Happy Fat Tuesday!
notes.content:
[img]http://raconteurgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/fat-tuesday-screenshot.jpg[/img]

From everyone at Raconteur, we'd like to wish all of you a very happy Mardi Gras! The final level in Story Hub 1, Fat Tuesday, is a Mardi Gras-themed level that lets you build a fleet... of Mardi Gras-style minions!

The level actually encapsulates the history of Mardi Gras more than you might think. In France, the event was originally used as a way of mocking the monarchy -- and in Close Order, you're making a fool of the Emperor's armada (from the third level of Story Hub 1, "Deck of Cards") with wacky parade ships!

If you ever looked at a parade and said, "That would be PERFECT in my fleet!" then you owe it to yourself to boot up Fat Tuesday today - especially since we now have trading cards!

There's never been a better time to join our community and experience our wonderfully odd little game. :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Trading Cards, Emoticons and More!
notes.content:
Happy Monday, everybody!

We hope you've been enjoying everything that Close Order has to offer. 

Since launch on January 21st, we've been hard at work to improve your experience. We've launched several updates improving the game over the past two weeks, and just a few of the things we've fixed since launch are:

[list]
    [*]Fixed issues with the opening scene not properly loading
    [*]Fixed all reported issues related to crashing
    [*]Eliminated a memory leak that was deteriorating performance
    [*]Improved hitboxes
    [*]Added health bar coloration to better convey when the player is about to die
    [*]Fixed resolution and user interface scaling issues in full-screen mode
[/list] 

In addition to this, we have several features planned for this month's 1.1 update!

[list]
    [*]Difficulty adjustments; our exact plans are not final, but we plan to improve the current experience based on a lot of feedback saying certain missions were too difficult
    [*]Audio options; we'll be adding the ability to adjust sound effects and music volume, in addition to master volume (and also fixing a bug where the options may not save)
    [*]Controller support (regular controllers, not specifically the Steam controller)
[/list] 

Finally, as of this post, [b]we have now added the full Steam Trading Card experience to Close Order![/b]

Try and collect all of the trading cards, badges, emoticons, and profile backgrounds that you can! They're pretty darn cool, if you ask us.

We're constantly listening to the community, and look forward to hearing what y'all think. Thanks for being great! :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Hotfix #2 is out!
notes.content:
Happy Saturday, folks!

We've uploaded a second small update for Close Order. It addresses the following:

[list]
    [*]Fixed crash in opening scene related to certain components being activated prematurely.
    [*]Fixed Shop and Formation Editor menus being accessible in cinematics.
    [*]Fixed kill counter tracking issues.
    [*]Fixed damage issue with enemy that fires lasers.
    [*]Made health bar visually reflect your status (orange and red coloration based on damage taken).
    [*]Solution for UI issues was to force native resolution in full screen mode. This is, unfortunately, a Unity issue we can't fix, and this is our best solution at the moment.
    [*]Made enemy bullets more visible.
    [*]Minor difficulty adjustments (major difficulty changes coming in 1.1)
    [*]Other various bug fixes and performance fixes.
[/list] 

Thank you to everyone who has been providing us feedback and helping us improve our game! Close Order now has more people playing than ever before, and we're finding more issues than we ever could have anticipated due to the volume of people playing -- and with your help, we'll keep making the game better.

notes.title: The Campfire: Gather 'round for news, and sign up for testing!
notes.content:
How's it going, badasses?

We wanted to pull you 'round the campfire for just a few minutes to discuss our plans.

In short: Close Order has been an exciting learning experience for us. We don't define success monetarily, but rather, based on us putting out a product that we're proud of. We're proud of the mashup that is Close Order, but we're listening to YOU to make it something you're proud to play.

We've learned a lot over the past two months. Quite a lot, in fact! All of this learning helped us identify a few key things:


[olist]
    [*]We needed to focus more on squashing bugs and ensuring quality.
    [*]We needed more content to allow you to be even more badass.
    [*]We needed to make sure you get genuine value out of Close Order.
[/olist] 

With this in mind, I wanted to announce our plans through the end of the year!


[list]
    [*]First, we've lowered the price to $4.99. We feel you get more value this way, and we want to thank those who've been with us since launch -- you've helped us learn so much!
    [*]Second, instead of jumping into more content right away, we decided to harness all of your feedback and tidy up our mechanics and overall design. We're still doing that, but we finally believe we're close to getting it right. We'll continue providing regular updates to fix bugs and improve the overall quality of the game.
    [*]Finally, it's that same question -- content! We're excited to announce that we're working on the remaining levels of hub world 1, and we're designing them in a very different fashion to reflect what we've learned from previous issues. There's no exact date on this content yet, but we hope to deliver it in a month or so.
[/list]

Soon, you'll be getting an update that further streamlines your experience and focuses on the core of what Close Order is: becoming a badass armada! In that update, we're revitalizing how we tell the story of Abe, Chakor and Mary, and we think you'll like the changes. More on that very soon.

LASTLY! If anyone would like to sign up to test forthcoming updates, please send an email to info@raconteurgames.com with the subject line "Update Tester" and we'll get you in on our playtest lists. Early Access is a great way to test new ideas, but we use playtests to get things up to a quality standard before we put things out there.

In summary, we've learned a lot. We're applying that learning to the game, and we've got some really, really exciting things coming that will make the game even better.

Keep being badass.

notes.title: The Campfire: Gather 'round for news, and sign up for testing!
notes.content:
How's it going, badasses?

We wanted to pull you 'round the campfire for just a few minutes to discuss our plans.

In short: Close Order has been an exciting learning experience for us. We don't define success monetarily, but rather, based on us putting out a product that we're proud of. We're proud of the mashup that is Close Order, but we're listening to YOU to make it something you're proud to play.

We've learned a lot over the past two months. Quite a lot, in fact! All of this learning helped us identify a few key things:


[olist]
    [*]We needed to focus more on squashing bugs and ensuring quality.
    [*]We needed more content to allow you to be even more badass.
    [*]We needed to make sure you get genuine value out of Close Order.
[/olist] 

With this in mind, I wanted to announce our plans through the end of the year!


[list]
    [*]First, we've lowered the price to $4.99. We feel you get more value this way, and we want to thank those who've been with us since launch -- you've helped us learn so much!
    [*]Second, instead of jumping into more content right away, we decided to harness all of your feedback and tidy up our mechanics and overall design. We're still doing that, but we finally believe we're close to getting it right. We'll continue providing regular updates to fix bugs and improve the overall quality of the game.
    [*]Finally, it's that same question -- content! We're excited to announce that we're working on the remaining levels of hub world 1, and we're designing them in a very different fashion to reflect what we've learned from previous issues. There's no exact date on this content yet, but we hope to deliver it in a month or so.
[/list]

Soon, you'll be getting an update that further streamlines your experience and focuses on the core of what Close Order is: becoming a badass armada! In that update, we're revitalizing how we tell the story of Abe, Chakor and Mary, and we think you'll like the changes. More on that very soon.

notes.title: Our First Big Early Access Update is LIVE!
notes.content:
Happy Friday!

We're pleased to announce that the Shmupdate, a fundamental revamp of our enemies and single player missions, is LIVE!

This is our first major update with Early Access, and with it comes a slew of changes that make the game way better. A lot of this feedback is a direct result of what YOU have told us! Here's a detailed breakdown.

[h1][b]General Changes[/b][/h1]

[list]
    [*]Single player missions reworked to be more fluid
    [*]Dialogue no longer pauses the game
    [*]Camera control no longer taken from the player
    [*]Emphasized story to be more focused on the briefings rather than in-level conversations (though those still happen)
    [*]Revamped enemies from the ground up (details in next section)
    [*]Minor minion adjustments to have more distinct counters to updated enemies
    [*]Molotok bullets now spin around perimeter of armada once after initial explosion
    [*]Various performance tweaks
    [*]Lots and lots of small things that overall make the game much better
[/list] 

[h1][b]Enemy Changes[/b][/h1]

The old enemies you know are gone, except for the models. Each of the new enemy types are listed below!

[h1]Swarmer[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Attacks in great swarms. Weak alone, but challenging in numbers!
[/list] 

[h1]Kamikaze[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Heavily armored foe that charges into the player and instantly explodes upon impact, causing great damage.
[/list] 

[h1]Broadsider[/h1]
[list]
    [*]A quick-moving ship that encircles the player, firing upon them while moving quickly.
[/list] 

[h1]Closer[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Enemy that aggressively closes on the player, shooting a powerful -- but inaccurate -- shot.
[/list] 

[h1]Bombarder[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Fires a solid beam of energy that deals damage every half-second.
[/list] 

[h1]Gunner[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Fires constant shots at the player to attempt to distract them from heavier or more deadly targets.
[/list] 

[h1]Grenadier[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Shoots an exploding projectile that can be deadly to large armadas!
[/list] 

[h1]Carrier Ship[/h1]
[list]
    [*]A large, heavily armed ship that can spawn smaller ships (such as the Swarmer).
[/list] 

Here's a glimpse of a test scene filled with Swarmers and Bombarders, with a Carrier Ship in the background.

They may not seem very tough...

[img]http://raconteurgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/boids2-2015-08-28-16-28-01-47.png[/img]

... but then BOOM!

[img]http://raconteurgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/boids2-2015-08-28-16-28-02-71.png[/img]

With this update, we've accomplished many things. Primarily, 1) we're more confident in our storytelling methods, and 2) we're more pleased with how enemies work and how minions counter them.

We'll continue updating the game with small bug fixes until our next big update: Those three other missions in hub world 1! 

We hope you enjoy Close Order even more than before with this big update. Early Access has been a lot of fun so far, and we have even more exciting things to come! Stay tuned, but for now... go be badass! :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Update on The Shmupdate
notes.content:
Hello again!

We've been working hard on our first big update to Close Order. Since we released August 7th, there has been a wealth of feedback and data on how we should improve the game.

We decided to be ambitious, and revamped every single enemy in the game from the ground up. The new enemies you'll face will be swift, deadly, and pose a much more serious challenge. Gone are the days of awkward enemy formations -- and now are the days of swarms, fleets, and armies of challenging foes!

The enemies may look the same, but their behaviors are completely rebuilt. The new enemies you will be facing:

[h1]MookShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Attacks in great swarms. Weak alone, but challenging in numbers!
[/list] 

[h1]SuicideShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Heavily armored foe that charges into the player and instantly explodes upon impact, causing great damage.
[/list] 

[h1]BroadsideShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]A quick-moving ship that encircles the player, firing upon them while moving quickly.
[/list] 

[h1]ShotgunShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Enemy that aggressively closes on the player, shooting a powerful -- but inaccurate -- shot.
[/list] 

[h1]BeamShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Fires a solid beam of energy that deals damage every half-second.
[/list] 

[h1]TurretShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Fires constant shots at the player to attempt to distract them from heavier or more deadly targets.
[/list] 

[h1]GrenadierShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Shoots an exploding projectile that can be deadly to large armadas!
[/list] 

[h1]CarrierShip[/h1]
[list]
    [*]A large, heavily armed ship that can spawn smaller ships (such as the MookShip).
[/list] 

Additionally, each ship has a clear rock-paper-scissors-style strength/weakness system with minions. This means minions have also been adjusted to more accurately reflect clear strengths/weaknesses, thus giving them even more importance.

Here's an example of a chaotic new scene in action:

It starts off simple enough...

[img]http://raconteurgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/boids2-2015-08-28-16-28-01-47.png[/img]

... but then these new foes ATTACK!

[img]http://raconteurgames.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/boids2-2015-08-28-16-28-02-71.png[/img]

There's a lot of love in this new update, and we think this will make Close Order exponentially better.

We'll be pushing a slight retooling of single-player levels as well to temporarily accommodate these new changes, but the update that follows this one will focus on improving how we tell our stories, and we've got equally exciting changes on that front.

Thank you all for sticking around and helping us make this game even more badass. It's paying off! Please keep sounding off and letting us know what you think, because it goes a very long way.

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Coming Soon: The Shmupdate!
notes.content:
Good evening, badasses!

Over the past several days, we've been looking at your feedback very seriously and coming up with a plan for our next steps to improve the game.

Our answer: [b]The Shmupdate[/b].

This is a massive update that will drop hopefully in early September. Essentially, it focuses on reworking and revitalizing our enemies to make them more deadly, challenging, and interesting to fight. 

As a result, it will place more importance on minions and armada variety -- a key part of Close Order that we feel could be emphasized further.

What we'll be doing is completely reworking their behavior and attack patterns, how they fight in groups, and what their strengths/weaknesses are.

No longer will you fight groups of formations -- you'll be fighting swarms (among many other kinds) of re-energized foes eager to annihilate your armada! Additionally, enemies will now be defined by their behavior rather than their narrative context.

These changes will more distinctly align the game with its core arcade-y, shoot-em-up (shmup) roots.

We don't have a definite date for this update to land, but we'll keep you posted. Tentatively, it's looking like early September.

Please continue telling us how you feel, because this is exactly how we make the game even better!

Finally, a sneak peak at other changes -- we're also working on improving how we tell stories within Close Order. We feel that there are even better ways to convey the journey of Mary, Abe, and Chakor in their pursuits of the remnants of humanity, and we're going to bring it to you very soon.

Again, thank you all for your patience and willingness to help us make Close Order better. :)

- The Raconteur Team

notes.title: Big Bug Fix #1 is LIVE!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Close Order has been available for a week now, and we've had a really fun time seeing your feedback and finding out how to make the game better.

We've been pushing small updates, but we just uploaded a patch that fixes a LOT of things and also adds some new features. If you haven't played in the past few days, here's what's new and updated:


[list]
    [*]Main menu now has a button to view the changelog
    [*]Tutorial bug that prevented you from advancing if you bought too many minions too early has been resolved
    [*]Minion consistency/saving across levels has been greatly improved
    [*]Added ability to swap two minions' positions on the Formation Editor
    [*]Issues with Scalprum damage on Volcano Ridge fixed
    [*]Audio fixes, and master volume option
    [*]Added a "minions bought" counter to the shop menu
    [*]Minions unlocked from story levels now save properly
    [*]Fixed Wandering Soul audio issues
    [*]Fixed bug on Black Hole that would not kill minions that were sucked into it
    [*]Fixed bug that allowed the player to shoot within a Crossroads hub
    [*]Various performance increases
[/list] 

We've made a LOT of progress thanks to your feedback. The number one thing we've added in, though...

[h1]Player death![/h1]

You may think that this was something that should have been in from the start -- we were thinking of alternative ways to approach this issue, since Close Order is far from a typical game. For now, it makes more sense to be able to die. As a result of that, we have given the player ship (Nadezhda) a small amount of health; the health bar in the lower right-hand corner of the screen now reflects the player ship's health, rather than the relative health of the entire armada (as it did previously). 

There are a lot of other little fixes too that we missed here, but all you need to know is this: Close Order will become even more badass with your help.

We've got some great things planned for this game, and we're so glad to be able to have you right here with us! Please continue telling us your thoughts on the forums so we can keep improving your experience.

Go be badass! :)

- The Raconteur Team
